BBC News | datePublished: 2026-10-23T23:08:23.210Z | dateModified: 2026-10-23T23:08:23.210Z

A student-led opposition movement is running neck-and-neck with Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić's ruling party ahead of Sunday's parliamentary elections, in the most serious electoral challenge to Vučić since his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) took power in 2012.

The "Student List" grew out of nearly two years of anti-corruption protests led by young Serbians, triggered by outrage over the deaths of 16 people when a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad, Serbia's second city. Rather than its organisers standing themselves, student-led assemblies at universities across the country selected 250 candidates to contest the election.

One of its leading figures is Ilija Srdanović, a cardiologist who has become the top candidate for the movement, campaigning as the most serious threat yet to Vučić's long rule. The vote takes place this Sunday, 25 October 2026, and is being closely watched as a test of whether the protest movement can translate street anger into parliamentary seats.
